correctness.rationale: The positive Fourier lines over a full time period are d₁,d₂,d₁+d₂. When distinct they reveal p=b₁ conjugate(b₀), q=b₂ conjugate(b₁) and r=b₂ conjugate(b₀); pq/r=|b₁|² determines a phase-fixed solution since all coefficients are nonzero. At resonance the trace gives the power spectrum of a quadratic P on the unit circle. For each off-circle reciprocal-conjugate root pair represented j times in the roots of P, the possible root multiplicities give j+1 choices; unit-circle multiplicities are fixed. The product is at most four even in repeated-root cases. The four witnesses have Fourier coefficients 62, −35 and 6 at 0,24,48, are inequivalent, and persist as four admissible classes under small perturbations of the two distinct nonreciprocal roots. At the second site the two contributions are multiplied by exp(im₁h), exp(im₂h) with m_j the adjacent spatial gaps. The determinant vanishes exactly at Δh∈2πZ; there the intensity is a time translate with shift m₁h/d, so the ambiguity survives. Otherwise the colliding products demix. The Gram eigenvalues are 2±2|cos(Δh/2)|; expanding the smaller gives inverse norm asymptotic 2/(|Δ||h−h₀|). This verifies product-demixing, not global nonlinear conditioning. CHECK.py was inspected, not executed; the review used Fourier identities and exact witnesses, not the file's finite test count.

value.rationale: For known three-mode data the result answers the operational question of where a second sensor is necessary, exactly which placements work for all allowed signals, and how ill-conditioned demixing becomes near a failed placement. The quantified ambiguity and open family show the failure is not an isolated exceptional vector. This is a natural exact classification without claiming stability at vanishing amplitudes or finite-time sampling optimality.
